title: A Yearbook for the Detention
premise: Felix Ravensworth, a senior at Hollow Creek High, bakes his unspoken grief for his late mother into bread no one can eat without crying — until the college essay prompt 'What is the truth you've never told?' unlocks a confession he can't take back: the yearbook detention room hides evidence that his father's bakery fire wasn't an accident. Pulled into an underground student tribunal called the Detention, Felix must argue his family's case before a jury of misfits while also competing in the state baking championship that could fund his escape from town. As the two contests collide, Felix learns that justice made by teenagers is as fragile as proof, and that memory is an inheritance you choose what to do with. He wins neither contest cleanly — but he wins the truth, reopens the fire investigation, and finally bakes bread that tastes like nothing but bread.
about_author: Odile Voss is a former debate coach and night-shift baker who writes young adult novels about kids who build their own courtrooms when the grown-up ones fail them. She lives above a shuttered bakery and insists the ovens still work.

chapters.title: The Bread That Made Mrs. Okafor Cry
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. At the bakery, Felix kneads his grief into a memorial loaf; teacher Mrs. Okafor eats a slice and weeps without knowing why. Establishes his gift, his silence about his mother, and the pressure of senior year. Emotional beat: tenderness disguised as routine.

chapters.title: Prompt Number Four
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. English class receives the college essay prompt: 'What is the truth you've never told?' Felix freezes, then writes three pages about the night of the bakery fire — and realizes mid-sentence he remembers a second set of footprints. Beat: the crack in the dam.

chapters.title: Detention Is Not Punishment Here
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Sentenced to Saturday detention for sleeping in class, Felix discovers Room 114 runs a secret student court called the Detention, presided over by razor-sharp Imogen Vale. They've read his essay — confiscated drafts circulate. Beat: wary fascination.

chapters.title: The Case of the Ravensworth Fire
chapters.summary: Imogen's POV. The Detention votes to hear Felix's case: arson, possibly involving his uncle Dale, who inherited half the bakery. Imogen privately doubts Felix's memory but needs a win to keep the court alive. Beat: ambition tangled with doubt.

chapters.title: Witnesses Who Were Twelve
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix and court clerk Priya track down childhood neighbors whose statements contradict the official report. One witness recants on her porch, terrified. Beat: first taste of how heavy other people's fear is.

chapters.title: Flour, Sugar, Deadline
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The state baking championship looms; Felix's entry must be 'a dessert that tells your story.' His father, fragile since the fire, begs him to drop it. Beat: guilt pulling him in two directions.

chapters.title: Imogen's Rules of Evidence
chapters.summary: Imogen's POV. Imogen trains Felix to testify, revealing her own motive: her brother was expelled on falsified evidence years ago. She teaches him that a case is a story with receipts. Beat: mentorship hardening into alliance.

chapters.title: The Uncle at the Funeral Dinner
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. At a family dinner, Felix probes Uncle Dale about the fire; Dale's alibi has a hole shaped like a locked storage room. Dad defends Dale fiercely. Beat: betrayal suspected inside the only family he has left.

chapters.title: Exhibit B: The Insurance Letter
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya finds a letter suggesting the insurance payout was contested — and that someone forged Dad's signature. The court celebrates; Felix feels sick that justice smells like paperwork. Beat: triumph shadowed by dread.

chapters.title: What the Bread Remembers
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Baking at 3 a.m., Felix realizes his gift works both ways: eating his bread surfaces buried memories. He bakes a batch for the recanting witness, who remembers seeing Dale's truck. Beat: grief weaponized, gently.

chapters.title: Opposing Counsel
chapters.summary: Imogen's POV. Star athlete Theo Marsh — whose father is the insurance adjuster — demands to defend Dale in the Detention's trial, turning the hearing adversarial. Imogen suspects sabotage. Beat: the court becomes a battlefield.

chapters.title: Midterms and Middle Grounds
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Grades slip, Dad's depression deepens, and Felix nearly quits the case after Dale quietly pays off the bakery's debts. Kindness as cover? Beat: the seduction of not knowing.

chapters.title: The Recantation
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Their key witness publicly denies everything in the school paper, and the Detention leaks Felix's essay as retaliation from someone inside. Trust fractures. Beat: betrayal within the sanctuary.

chapters.title: Imogen Falls
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Imogen is suspended from school over planted evidence — the same trick used on her brother. With the court leaderless, Felix must decide whether the Detention was ever real or just her. Beat: despair and resolve colliding.

chapters.title: A Courtroom of Misfits
chapters.summary: Ensemble chapter, Felix's POV. The Detention members refuse to disband; Felix, reluctantly, takes the chair. They rebuild the case from scratch, discovering the forged signature matches Theo's father's handwriting samples. Beat: found family under pressure.

chapters.title: The Championship Round
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. At states, Felix presents his story-dessert — a burnt-honey tart layered like testimony — and chokes during judging when he sees Dale in the audience. He advances anyway, hollowly. Beat: victory that tastes like ash.

chapters.title: Dale's Confession, Sort Of
chapters.summary: Dale's POV (first non-Felix intimate view). Cornered by Felix with the handwriting evidence, Dale admits he was there that night — covering for Dad, whose debt-fueled desperation started the fire Dale failed to stop. Beat: the villain dissolves into tragedy.

chapters.title: The Trial of Room 114
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The full Detention convenes its climactic hearing with Theo cross-examining. Felix must choose between destroying his father or telling the whole truth. He testifies to everything, including Dad's role. Beat: the honest question answered at last.

chapters.title: Verdicts We Can't Enforce
chapters.summary: Imogen's POV. The court finds Dale negligent but Dad responsible; they deliver the verdict to the real authorities, knowing teens have no power to compel anything. Imogen's suspension is overturned when the forgery surfaces. Beat: justice offered, not guaranteed.

chapters.title: Finals Day
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The championship final coincides with Dad turning himself in. Felix bakes his last competition piece — plain sourdough, his mother's recipe, no feelings hidden — and loses first place. He doesn't care. Beat: release.

chapters.title: What Gets Inherited
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Visiting Dad before sentencing, Felix brings bread and forgiveness that isn't absolution. Dale signs the bakery over to Felix. The essay gets submitted, unchanged, all three pages. Beat: inheritance reclaimed on his own terms.

chapters.title: Room 114, Next September
chapters.summary: Ensemble epilogue, alternating POVs. The Detention formally adopts a constitution; Felix passes the gavel to Priya and leaves for culinary school with Imogen driving him to the bus. The last line: the oven is preheating, and everything might actually be fine. Beat: hopeful, earned quiet.
